questions.q: What is a "circuit," as this lesson defines it?
options: A specific subgraph of a model's actual weights/components -- particular heads, neurons, or residual-stream directions -- that together implement an identifiable algorithm or behavior
Any visualization of a model's attention weights
A diagram drawn by a researcher with no connection to the model's real weights
The full set of all parameters in a neural network
questions.explain: A circuit is a real, traceable computational pathway through the model's actual parameters, not a metaphor or a purely illustrative diagram.

questions.q: Which paper introduced the residual-stream framing this lesson relies on?
options: "Attention Is All You Need"
The original BERT paper
"A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits" (Elhage et al., 2021)
"Toy Models of Superposition"
questions.explain: Elhage et al.'s 2021 Mathematical Framework paper proposed treating the residual stream as a shared communication channel that heads and MLPs read from and write to additively.

questions.q: Why does the additive structure of the residual stream make circuit analysis tractable?
options: Because it removes the need for any forward hooks or activation capture
Because every head/MLP's contribution is summed in, each component can be treated as acting independently, turning one impenetrable function into a sum of inspectable pieces
It doesn't -- the residual stream makes analysis harder, not easier
Because the residual stream deletes all information except the final layer's output
questions.explain: Since contributions are additive, a given head's effect doesn't have to be untangled from every other head's effect first -- it can be inspected on its own.

questions.q: In the lesson's forward-hook code, why is the attention block's output reshaped to `(batch, seq, num_heads, d_head)`?
options: Reshaping has no functional purpose in this code
Because the attention block internally concatenates all heads' outputs before its output projection, so reshaping recovers each individual head's own slice
To convert the activations into a different data type
To delete every head except the first one
questions.explain: The combined `(batch, seq, d_model)` output is actually every head's contribution concatenated together; reshaping splits it back into one slice per head.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish mechanistic circuit analysis from the probing-classifier approach covered in Chapter 5?
options: Probing classifiers are only used on vision models, never on language models
Circuit analysis never uses any form of activation inspection
Probing asks what correlates with what in a model's representations; circuit analysis asks which specific weights and components causally compute a behavior
There is no meaningful difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: The lesson frames mechanistic interpretability as going beyond correlational probing toward identifying the actual computational pathway responsible for a behavior.
